newsitem.title: HONG KONG: TVB forecasts 1997 earnings turnaround.
newsitem.headline: TVB forecasts 1997 earnings turnaround.

text.p: Television Broadcasts Ltd (TVB) said the downturn in consumer spending in Hong Kong has bottomed out and the company's prospects for 1997 are much improved.
"As the general economic recovery gains momentum, we anticipate increases in television advertising expenditures," the company said in its 1996 results announcement released on Wednesday.

The broadcasting and production company reported profit attributable to shareholders for the year ended December 31, 1996, of HK$477.2 million, a drop of 1.72 percent compared with 1995's HK$485.55 million.
Given an improvement in its already high ratings, the company should be the primary beneficiary of the recovery in the television advertising market, the statement said.
"Accordingly, we anticipate a rebound in earnings for 1997," the statement said.
TVB said it anticipated continued growth in demand for its output of Chinese-language programmes through its international licensing and distribution businesses in Asia.

The broadcaster, which claims to be the world's largest producer of Chinese-language programming, also said it would benefit as more terrestrial, cable and satellite television services came on line throughout the region.
Reflecting on 1996, the company said growth in revenue had been restrained by a slowdown in advertising spending.
"The performance of Hong Kong's television industry in general continued to be constrained by an ongoing slowdown in consumer spending and an attendant reduction in advertising outlays," it said.
Earnings per share fell to HK$1.14, compared with HK$1.16 in the previous year.
The company maintained its dividend payout, announcing a final dividend of HK$0.60 which together with the interim dividend of HK$0.20 yielded a total dividend of HK$0.80, unchanged from last year.
